questions.question: What is the third proportional to 16 and 48?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Numbers in continued proportion maintain a constant multiplying ratio between consecutive terms.

Multiplying factor = Second term ÷ First term = 48 ÷ 16 = 3

Third term = Second term × Multiplying factor

Third term = 48 × 3 = 144

**∴ The correct answer is 144.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First term (a) = 16

Second term (b) = 48

**Formula Used:**

If c is the third proportional to a and b, then a : b = b :

questions.question: If at same rate of interest, in 2 years, the simple interest is ₹42 and compound interest is ₹51, then what is the principal (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

SI for 1 year = 42 ÷ 2 = ₹21

CI − SI difference for 2 years = 51 − 42 = ₹9

Rate % = (Difference ÷ 1st year SI) × 100 = (9 ÷ 21) × 100 = 300/7%

Principal = (1st year SI × 100) ÷ Rate %

Principal = (21 × 100) ÷ (300/7) = 21 × 7/3 = ₹49

**∴ The correct answer is ₹49.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) for 2 years = ₹42

Compound Interest (CI) for 2 years = ₹51

**Formula Used:**

SI for 1 year = Total SI ÷ Time

Difference (CI − SI) for 2 years = Interest on first year's SI

questions.question: Determine the largest four-digit number that is exactly divisible by 15, 25, 40, and 75.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The required number must be perfectly divisible by 15, 25, 40, and 75.

The LCM of 25 and 40 is 200, so any such common multiple must end with two zeros.

Among the given options (9600, 9960, 9975, and 9999), only 9600 ends with two zeros.

Also, 9600 is fully divisible by 15 and 75.

**∴ The correct answer is 9600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers: 15, 25, 40, and 75

**Concept Used:**

To find the largest number of a given number of digits divisible by a set of numbers, subtract the remainder when the largest possible number is divided by their LCM.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 15 = 3 × 5

⇒ Prime factorization of 25 = 5²

⇒ Prime factorization of 40 = 2³ × 5

⇒ Prime factorization of 75 = 3 × 5²

⇒ LCM of (15, 25, 40, 75) = 2³ × 3 × 5²

⇒ LCM = 8 × 3 × 25 = 600

⇒ The largest four-digit number is 9999.

⇒ Now, divide 9999 by the LCM (600):

⇒ 9999 ÷ 600 = 16 with a remainder of 399.

⇒ Required number = Largest 4-digit number − Remainder

⇒ Required number = 9999 − 399 = 9600

**∴ The correct answer is 9600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The LCM of two or more numbers is the smallest number which is completely divisible by each of the given numbers without leaving a remainder.

Smallest n-digit Number Divisible by given numbers

To find the smallest n-digit number perfectly divisible by a set of numbers, use the formula: Required = Smallest n-digit Number + (LCM − Remainder).

Divisibility Rule of 25 and 40

A number is divisible by 25 if its last two digits are 00, 25, 50, or 75. A number is divisible by 40 if it is simultaneously divisible by both 5 and 8.
</p

questions.question: The average weight of Gopal, Akshay and Atul is 46 kg . If the average weight of Gopal and Akshay be 40 kg and that of Akshay and Atul be 45 kg, then the weight of Akshay (in kg) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total weight of all 3 persons = 3 × 46 = 138 kg.

Combined sum of the 2 overlapping pairs = (2 × 40) + (2 × 45) = 80 + 90 = 170 kg.

Akshay is counted twice in the sum of these two pairs.

⇒ Akshay's weight = Combined sum of pairs − Total weight of all 3

⇒ Akshay's weight = 170 − 138 = 32 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 32 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average weight of Gopal, Akshay, and Atul = 46 kg

Average weight of Gopal and Akshay = 40 kg

Average weight of Akshay and Atul = 45 kg

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 Total = 138 kg

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 G + A = 80 kg

 
 Gopal (G)

 
 Akshay (A)

 
 Atul (T)

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 A + T = 90 kg

 Akshay = (80 + 90) − 138 = 32 kg

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of Gopal + Akshay + Atul = 46 × 3 = 138 kg ... (i)

⇒ Total weight of Gopal + Akshay = 40 × 2 = 80 kg ... (ii)

⇒ Total weight of Akshay + Atul = 45 × 2 = 90 kg ... (iii)

From equation (i) and (ii), we can find the weight of Atul:

⇒ Atul = Total weight − (Gopal + Akshay)

⇒ Atul = 138 − 80 = 58 kg

Substitute Atul's weight in equation (iii):

⇒ Akshay + 58 = 90

⇒ Akshay = 90 − 58 = 32 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 32 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Formula

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations.

Overlapping Groups

If the sum of parts exceeds the sum of the whole, the overlapping element is the exact difference between the combined parts and the total sum.

Net Deviation Method

The sum of deviations of all given observations from their exact true average is always zero.
</p

questions.question: In an examination, there were three papers of Mathematics, two papers of English and one paper of Science. All papers were of 100 marks. S got 60% in Mathematics, 70% in English and 50% in Science. What was his percentage of marks in all papers?

Using the weighted average method for percentage over the ratio of the number of papers:

Ratio of papers = 3 (Maths) : 2 (English) : 1 (Science)

Overall Percentage = (3 × 60% + 2 × 70% + 1 × 50%) ÷ (3 + 2 + 1)

⇒ Overall Percentage = (180% + 140% + 50%) ÷ 6 = 370% ÷ 6

⇒ Overall Percentage ≈ 61.67%

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 32 days and B in 48 days. They work together for 8 days and then A goes away. In how much time (in days) will B finish the 60% of the remaining work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Total Work = LCM of 32 and 48 = 96 units.

Efficiency of A = 3, Efficiency of B = 2 → Combined = 5 units/day.

Work done by A and B in 8 days = 8 × 5 = 40 units.

Remaining work = 96 − 40 = 56 units.

Time required for B to finish 60% of remaining work = (56 × 60/100) ÷ 2 = 33.6 ÷ 2 = 16.8 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 ⁴/₅ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A to complete the work = 32 days

Time taken by B to complete the work = 48 days

A and B worked together for 8 days.

**Calculations:**

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 32
 96
 3
 
 

 B
 48
 2
 
 

⇒ Total combined efficiency of A and B = 3 + 2 = 5 units/day

⇒ Work completed by A and B in 8 days = 8 × 5 = 40 units

⇒ Remaining work = 96 − 40 = 56 units

⇒ 60% of the remaining work = (60 / 100) × 56 = 33.6 units

⇒ Time taken by B to complete this 60% work = Work ÷ Efficiency of B

⇒ Time taken by B = 33.6 ÷ 2 = 16.8 days

⇒ 16.8 days = 16 ⁸/₁₀ days = 16 ⁴/₅ days

**∴ The correct answer is 16 ⁴/₅ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM Method for Time & Work

Assuming the total work as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the given individual days makes the calculations fraction-free. The efficiency is simply Total Work ÷ Number of Days.

Work & Efficiency Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time. A highly efficient person will take less time to finish the work. Work done = Efficiency × Time.

Leaving Mid-way Problems

Calculate the total work completed during the combined working period, subtract it from the total assumed work, and assign the remainder entirely to the remaining active workers.
</p

questions.question: The LCM of 28, 60, 120 and 135 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The LCM must be exactly divisible by all the given numbers: 28, 60, 120, and 135.

Since 135 = 27 × 5, the LCM must be a multiple of 5 (ending in 0 or 5) and 9 (sum of digits is a multiple of 9).

From the given options, 7626, 7569, and 7608 do not end in 0 or 5, so they are not divisible by 5.

Only 7560 ends in 0, and its digit sum is 7 + 5 + 6 + 0 = 18, which is divisible by 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 7560.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 28, 60, 120, and 135.

**Method Used:**

Prime factorization method to find the Least Common Multiple (LCM).

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 28 = 2² × 7

⇒ Prime factorization of 60 = 2² × 3 × 5

⇒ Prime factorization of 120 = 2³ × 3 × 5

⇒ Prime factorization of 135 = 3³ × 5

⇒ The LCM is the product of the highest powers of all prime factors involved.

⇒ LCM = 2³ × 3³ × 5¹ × 7¹

⇒ LCM = 8 × 27 × 5 × 7

⇒ LCM = 40 × 189

⇒ LCM = 7560

**∴ The correct answer is 7560.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Prime Factorization Method

To find the LCM, express each number as a product of prime factors and multiply the highest power of each distinct prime factor present.

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is a multiple of 9. This helps eliminate wrong options quickly in LCM and HCF problems.

HCF and LCM Relation

For any two numbers a and b, the product of their HCF and LCM is strictly equal to the product of the numbers themselves: HCF × LCM = a × b.
</p

questions.question: A dishonest shopkeeper promises to sell his goods at cost price. However, he uses a weight that actually weighs 46% less than what is written on it. Find his profit percentage.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a dishonest shopkeeper selling at Cost Price (CP) but using false weights:

Profit % = [Error ÷ (Promised Weight − Error)] × 100

Profit % = [46 ÷ (100 − 46)] × 100

Profit % = (46 ÷ 54) × 100 = 2300 ÷ 27

**∴ The correct answer is 85 ⁵/₂₇ %.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The shopkeeper promises to sell his goods at cost price.

He uses a weight that is 46% less than the marked weight.

**Formula Used:**

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

 
 
 
 54% (Given)
 46% (Stolen)
 

 Cost Price (CP)
 

 Selling Price (SP) = 100% promised

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the true weight be 100 units and the price of 1 unit be &rupee;1.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) of promised 100 units = &rupee;100

⇒ Weight actually given = 100 − 46 = 54 units

⇒ Cost Price (CP) for shopkeeper = Price of 54 units = &rupee;54

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 100 − 54 = &rupee;46

⇒ Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (46 ÷ 54) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (23 ÷ 27) × 100 = 2300 ÷ 27

⇒ Profit % = 85 ⁵/₂₇ %

**∴ The correct answer is 85 ⁵/₂₇ %.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Principle

When a shopkeeper claims to sell goods at the cost price but uses a faulty weight, the profit is generated solely from the weight stolen. The formula is: Profit % = (True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight × 100.

Combined Profit (Markup + False Weight)

If a dealer marks up the price by P% and also uses a false weight that is W% less, the effective profit ratio can be evaluated using: SP / CP = (100 + P) / (100 − W).

Successive Percentage Change

When multiple percentage changes occur sequentially (e.g., markup then discount), the net percentage change is given by: Net change = x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100.
</p

questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio of 4 : 9. If the mean proportional between them is 24, find the positive difference between the two numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the two numbers be in the ratio parts 4x and 9x.

Mean proportional = √(4x × 9x) = √(36x²) = 6x.

Since the mean proportional is 24, we get 6x = 24 ⇒ x = 4.

Positive difference between the numbers = 9x − 4x = 5x.

Difference = 5 × 4 = 20.

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of the two numbers = 4 : 9

Mean proportional between the numbers = 24

**Formula Used:**

Mean proportional between a and b = √(a × b)

 
 Number 1 = 4x

 
 Number 2 = 9x

 

 
 Mean Prop = 6x = 24

 

 
 Difference = 5x = 20

**Calculations:**

Let the two numbers be 4x and 9x.

⇒ Mean proportional = √(4x × 9x)

⇒ √(36x²) = 24

⇒ 6x = 24

⇒ x = 24 ÷ 6

⇒ x = 4

⇒ First number = 4 × 4 = 16

⇒ Second number = 9 × 4 = 36

⇒ Positive difference = 36 − 16 = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional of two quantities a and b is given by √(a × b). It represents the value x where a : x = x : b.

Third Proportional

The third proportional to numbers a and b is a value c such that a : b = b : c. It is calculated using the formula c = b² ÷ a.

Fourth Proportional

The fourth proportional to numbers a, b, and c is a value d such that a : b = c : d. It is computed as d = (b × c) ÷ a.
</p

questions.question: Two cones have their heights in the ratio 4 : 3 and the radii of their bases in the ratio 1 : 2. Find the ratio of their volumes.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Volume of a cone (V) is proportional to r² × h.

Given r₁ : r₂ = 1 : 2 and h₁ : h₂ = 4 : 3.

Ratio of volumes = (1² × 4) : (2² × 3)

V₁ : V₂ = 4 : (4 × 3) = 4 : 12 = 1 : 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Ratio of heights (h₁ : h₂) = 4 : 3

Given: Ratio of radii (r₁ : r₂) = 1 : 2

Formula: Volume of cone (V) = (1/3) × π × r² × h

 

 
 
• 
 h1=4x
 
• 
 r1=1y
 

 
 
• 
 h2=3x
 
• 
 r2=2y
 Cone 1
 Cone 2

⇒ V₁ / V₂ = [(1/3) × π × r₁² × h₁] / [(1/3) × π × r₂² × h₂]

⇒ V₁ / V₂ = (r₁ / r₂)² × (h₁ / h₂)

⇒ V₁ / V₂ = (1 / 2)² × (4 / 3)

⇒ V₁ / V₂ = (1 / 4) × (4 / 3)

⇒ V₁ / V₂ = 4 / 12 = 1 / 3

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cone

The volume is exactly one-third the volume of a cylinder with same base and height: V = (1/3)πr²h.

Slant Height

The slant height (l) is the distance from the apex to any point on the base circle: l = √(r² + h²).

Surface Area

Curved Surface Area = πrl and Total Surface Area = πr(l + r).</p

questions.question: Mandar has two grandsons Ketan and Tushar. 11 year old Ketan gets some money from Mandar's wealth and 12 year old Tushar gets rest of the money. But Ketan and Tushar will get money only when they turn 22 years old. Till then the money is in a bank getting interest at rate 8% compounded annually. When both turn 22, they receive the same amount. How much had Mandar given Tushar (in ₹) initially, if total money with Mandar was ₹24700?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ketan's investment time = 22 − 11 = 11 years, and Tushar's investment time = 22 − 12 = 10 years.

Since they receive equal amounts at age 22, the ratio of their principals is inverse to the ratio of their compounding multipliers.

Tushar's share : Ketan's share = (1 + 8/100)¹¹−¹⁰ : 1 = 1.08 : 1 = 108 : 100 = 27 : 25.

Total ratio parts = 27 + 25 = 52 parts, which corresponds to the total wealth of ₹24700.

Tushar's share = (27 ÷ 52) × 24700 = 27 × 475 = ₹12825.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12825.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total initial money with Mandar = ₹24700

Ketan's age = 11 years, Tushar's age = 12 years

Target age for receiving the amount = 22 years

Rate of interest (R) = 8% compounded annually

 
 

 

 

 Investment Timeline & Growth

 
• 

 
 Ketan (11 yrs)
 ₹ K

 
 Tushar (12 yrs)
 ₹ T

 
 Age 22
 Amount Equal

 

 Time = 11 Years @ 8%

 

 Time = 10 Years @ 8%
 
 Total Wealth = ₹24700 (K + T)

**Formula Used:**

Compound Interest Amount = P(1 + R/100)T

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time duration for Ketan's investment = 22 − 11 = 11 years.

⇒ Time duration for Tushar's investment = 22 − 12 = 10 years.

⇒ Let Ketan's initial share be K and Tushar's initial share be T.

⇒ According to the problem, amounts received by both at age 22 are equal.

⇒ K(1 + 8/100)¹¹ = T(1 + 8/100)¹⁰

⇒ Dividing both sides by (1 + 8/100)¹⁰:

⇒ K(1 + 8/100)¹ = T

⇒ T / K = (100 + 8) / 100 = 108 / 100 = 27 / 25

⇒ The ratio of Tushar's share to Ketan's share is 27 : 25.

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 27 + 25 = 52 parts.

⇒ Total value of 52 parts = ₹24700

⇒ Value of 1 part = 24700 ÷ 52 = ₹475

⇒ Amount given to Tushar initially (T) = 27 parts = 27 × 475 = 12825.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12825.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equal Amount Distribution in CI

If an amount is divided between two individuals such that their shares become equal after t₁ and t₂ years respectively at R% compound interest, the ratio of their initial shares is P₁ : P₂ = (1 + R/100)t² − t¹.

Compound Interest Formula

The amount A after time T with principal P and rate R% compounded annually is given by the equation A = P(1 + R/100)T.

Rule of Present Value

When final future values are equal, the person who has a shorter time period for the money to grow requires a larger initial principal (Present Value) to reach the identical target amount.

questions.question: A man goes to Ahmedabad from Kolkata at a speed of 9 km/hr and returns to Kolkata at speed of 18 km/hr, through same route. What is his average speed (in km/hr) of the entire journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When equal distances are covered in both directions at speeds x and y, Average Speed = (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y)

Here, outward speed x = 9 km/hr and return speed y = 18 km/hr.

⇒ Average Speed = (2 × 9 × 18) ÷ (9 + 18)

⇒ Average Speed = 324 ÷ 27 = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

questions.question:
A student was getting the following four offers on the purchase of a book:

I - Two successive discounts of 20% and 20%

II - Two successive discounts of 25% and 15%

III - Two successive discounts of 30% and 10%

lV - Two successive discounts of 5% and 35%

Which scheme offers the most discount to the student?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the sum of two successive discounts is constant, the effective discount is maximized when their numerical difference is maximum.

The sum of the discounts in all four schemes is exactly 40%.

Difference for each scheme: I = 0%, II = 10%, III = 20%, IV = 30%.

Scheme IV has the maximum difference (35% − 5% = 30%), hence it provides the maximum effective discount.

**∴ The correct answer is Scheme IV.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Four schemes of successive discounts on a book.

**Formula Used:**

Effective discount for two successive discounts a% and b% = [a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100]%

 Effective Discount Comparison
 Scheme I
 
 36%
 Scheme II
 
 36.25%
 Scheme III
 
 37%
 Scheme IV
 
 38.25% (Max)
 
• 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Effective discount for Scheme I = 20 + 20 − (20 × 20) ÷ 100

⇒ Scheme I = 40 − 4 = 36%

⇒ Effective discount for Scheme II = 25 + 15 − (25 × 15) ÷ 100

⇒ Scheme II = 40 − 3.75 = 36.25%

⇒ Effective discount for Scheme III = 30 + 10 − (30 × 10) ÷ 100

⇒ Scheme III = 40 − 3 = 37%

⇒ Effective discount for Scheme IV = 35 + 5 − (35 × 5) ÷ 100

⇒ Scheme IV = 40 − 1.75 = 38.25%

⇒ Comparing all the calculated effective discounts, 38.25% is the maximum overall discount.

**∴ The correct answer is Scheme IV.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two consecutive discounts of a% and b% are applied on a marked price, the net effective discount is given by the formula: (a + b − a×b÷100)%.

Maximizing Effective Discount

If the sum of multiple successive discounts is constant, the overall discount is highest when the product of the individual discounts is minimized. This occurs when their numerical difference is maximum.

Marked Price & Selling Price

A discount is always calculated over the Marked Price (MP). The Selling Price (SP) after a discount of d% is evaluated as SP = MP × (100 − d)÷100.

Buy X Get Y Free

A widely used alternative discounting model. The effective discount percentage equals (Free items ÷ Total items) × 100.

questions.question: The price (per litre) of petrol increases by 85%. By what percent should its consumption be reduced such that the expenditure on it increases by 48% only?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the initial expenditure be 100.

Expenditure corresponding to the new price = 100 + 85 = 185.

Allowed expenditure = 100 + 48 = 148.

Reduction needed in consumption = 185 − 148 = 37.

Percentage reduction = (37 ÷ 185) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Increase in petrol price = 85%

Maximum allowed increase in expenditure = 48%

**Formula Used:**

Expenditure = Price × Consumption

Consumption = Expenditure ÷ Price

 
•

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the original price be ₹100 and original consumption be 100 litres.

⇒ Original Expenditure = 100 × 100 = 10000

⇒ New Price = 100 + 85% of 100 = ₹185

⇒ New Expenditure = 10000 + 48% of 10000 = 14800

⇒ New Consumption = New Expenditure ÷ New Price

⇒ New Consumption = 14800 ÷ 185 = 80 litres

⇒ Decrease in consumption = Original − New = 100 − 80 = 20 litres

⇒ Percentage decrease = (20 ÷ 100) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

Price and Consumption Rule

If the price of a commodity increases by x%, the reduction in consumption to keep expenditure constant is given by [x ÷ (100 + x)] × 100%. In cases where expenditure also changes, direct base scaling is preferred.

Successive Percentage Change

Net percentage change when two changes a% and b% are applied successively is calculated as: a + b + (a × b ÷ 100).

Base Change Method

Whenever expenditure changes along with price, shift the base to the new price equivalent (e.g., 185) and calculate the difference with the desired expenditure (e.g., 148) to easily spot the required percentage drop.

questions.question: The HCF of two numbers is 11 and their sum is 132. If both the numbers are greater than 42, then the difference between the two numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the numbers be 11x and 11y (where x, y are co-prime).

Sum = 11(x + y) = 132 ⇒ x + y = 12

Valid co-prime pairs for sum 12 are (1, 11) and (5, 7).

For (5, 7), the numbers are 55 and 77 (since both must be > 42).

Difference = 77 − 55 = 22

**∴ The correct answer is 22.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

HCF of the two numbers = 11

Sum of the two numbers = 132

Condition: Both numbers are greater than 42

**Formula Used:**

Any two numbers can be written as (HCF × a) and (HCF × b), where a and b are co-prime integers.

 Sum = 132 | HCF = 11
 
 Number 1
 
 11 × 5 = 55
 
 Number 2
 
 11 × 7 = 77
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 

 

 Diff = 22

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the two numbers be 11a and 11b, where a and b are co-prime.

⇒ Sum of the numbers = 11a + 11b = 132

⇒ 11(a + b) = 132

⇒ a + b = 132 ÷ 11 = 12

⇒ The possible integer pairs of (a, b) whose sum is 12 are: (1, 11), (2, 10), (3, 9), (4, 8), (5, 7), and (6, 6).

⇒ Since a and b must be co-prime (having no common factor other than 1), the valid pairs are (1, 11) and (5, 7).

⇒ Case 1: If a = 1 and b = 11 ⇒ The numbers are (11 × 1) = 11 and (11 × 11) = 121. (Rejected because 11 is not greater than 42).

⇒ Case 2: If a = 5 and b = 7 ⇒ The numbers are (11 × 5) = 55 and (11 × 7) = 77. (Accepted because both 55 and 77 are greater than 42).

⇒ The difference between the two numbers = 77 − 55 = 22.

**∴ The correct answer is 22.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime if their Highest Common Factor (HCF) is exactly 1. When dividing two numbers by their HCF, the resulting quotients must always be co-prime.

Relation between HCF and LCM

For any two numbers, the product of their HCF and LCM is strictly equal to the product of the numbers themselves: HCF × LCM = Number₁ × Number₂.

LCM Formula from Ratios

If two numbers are in the ratio a : b (where a and b are co-prime), their Least Common Multiple (LCM) is calculated directly as HCF × a × b.
